title: Sant Antoni: A Leisure Spot
subtitle: Researchers monitored people's activities while they rested, shopped or walked in the streets of Barcelona. Very few were doing strenuous physical activity.
excerpt: Researchers monitored people's activities while they rested, shopped or walked in the streets of Barcelona. Very few were doing strenuous physical activity.

content.alt: People sit on benches beside planters while others walk through the painted street space in Sant Antoni, Barcelona.
content.caption: People sitting and walking in the Sant Antoni superblock, Barcelona, May 28, 2022.

content.text: More than 900 people an hour used the Sant Antoni superblock during the observation period of a study published in 2025. People were resting or casually walking along the pedestrian zone.

Many older people, relatively few young people. Some chose the location because they found it pleasant. Some vehicles exceeded the 10 km/h limit, though families found it easier to walk about. Parents appreciated the zone but were concerned about traffic.

In Horta, cars stopped on the former sidewalks of the main entrance street, leaving pedestrians to walk around them. Some felt less safe, especially when accompanied by a child. Despite the level pavement, drivers behaved as though they had priority.

Cleaning the pedestrian zones brought another problem: crews struggled to work amid heavy foot traffic, according to a May 2026 City of Barcelona assessment of green corridors. Benches and other street furniture also made it hard to find room for bins. Although there were fewer bins, residents felt there were more. City authorities linked this perception to bins being placed along blocks rather than at street corners.

citations.text: Barcelona City Council. Funcionament del Pla de millora dels eixos verds. Public information session, May 18, 2026; especially pages 23–30 and the action plan.
